tips.comment: George Darling took a big step forward last time winning well over 2 mile 5 Furlong. He's a strong traveller, handles the ground and could still be improving. He's a big player.
Shaped encouragingly last time after 5 months off, and stepping back up in trip seems sure to suit as he got outpaced last time before running on. Drops a pound up in trip, decent chance.

This lad showed that the fire still flickers, at least last time out at Wetherby, and has a chance here off a feather bottom weight under a good conditional. With his yard in good form and with a good long-term record here, he has better form than the field on the forecasted ground, and the circumstances of the run are right for him.

This horse's 2nd over C&D is the piece of form which makes her of real interest here. The regular stable jockey takes over now, and he has a great record at this course. The subsequent runs of the winner and the well-beaten 5th, in particular, give this horse a huge chance, and that obvious liking for the course is a huge positive around here.
Out of an Ifraaj mare, and that is the most classy name being brought to the table in this race. Hurdles plus classiest broodmare stallion on show should equal going very close.
7lb below last winning mark and has run some decent races at big odds. Not the most consistent but does seem to retain ability. Looks too big a price to not have each-way interest.

Sonning has achieved more over hurdles than on the flat, admittedly a couple of years ago when he won rated 114h. He has had a spin around Pontefract 11 days ago over 12 furlongs, which should have blown away a few cobwebs. If a return to this discipline is straightforward, he is well handicapped on old form.
A tough individual, this one has not finished out of the frame in its last 6 outings, winning 2 of them. It is away from its favorite track of Southwell, but another who should cope well.
Dappled Light runs here off the back of a break and is a few pounds lighter than the market leader, which should be enough if fit enough for this.

Ran well to win over 9.5f here in January and was beaten less than a length when finishing second over the same track and trip three weeks later and wasn't beaten far when finishing just outside the places in fifth over the same track and trip last month. Drop back in trip should suit. Should be thereabouts.
Wyvern is still 1lb below last winning mark. Not been in good form lately but is capable of winning this if finding some form again.

Not an easy one to unravel and there's quite a few with questions next to them, even after decent recent runs. This 9yo Gale Force Ten gelding comes over from Ireland with some indifferent recent form, but on his past efforts he clearly has a shout at this level, and this is his trip. Is now weighted very lightly and has a capable 5 pound claimer aboard, so if not now, when..?
Won over today's course and distance in March and was a good 3rd last time out here again over course and distance. Expected to go well again, and in an open race, shouldn't be far away.

A 4-time career winner, the last 3 have all come on the AW between 7f and 1m1f. Staying on when only beaten 2 lengths over 7f at Southwell last time out 15 days ago, and should do better now back up in trip this afternoon.
Returns after 5 months off. 2/12 here in October by less than 1L C&D. Apprentice race with 5 lb claimer seems to go well in these events. Has a good draw in 3.
Firmly at the bottom of the handicap mark with a 3lb claimer, but also a 3-time C&D winner. Dropping down in class and hoping the use of blinkers can break the shocking run of form.

REBEL COVE has some high rated runners in her family and is bred to appreciate tonight's stiffer test of stamina. She starts out life handicapping from a lowly mark and interesting to see if she attracts any support.
Jolly Roger had a good win by 3L in December and is carrying a bit more weight today. However, he has a 2000 Guineas entry, which makes me think more is expected and could go well again.
Warrior Mode won on return to the track and should come on for the run. His main danger is the market leader who is returning to the track and may not be as ready as the selection was.

Related to a couple of winners on the all-weather tracks, Ed Walker’s trained colt should be good enough to defy a penalty for a novice event victory at Goodwood twelve months ago. Particularly, Red Sand runs well fresh judging by his runner-up effort on debut.

Ralph Beckett's 3yo New Approach gelding ran twice last season in, what are in hindsight, a couple of pretty warm events, finishing third on both occasions. Latterly, when benefiting from debut experience and beaten 2 lengths in a maiden over 8f at Goodwood. Has the top course jockey on board and back down in trip, looks to have at least good each-way claims on Tapeta debut.
Wave Rider hasn't been on the track for 6 months, but there's every reason to think the horse will improve after some good initial efforts. The form of some of the others isn't exactly sparkling.

This Blue Point colt is a half-brother to 3 successful racehorses including the capable Bowland Park, who has won up to 1 and a quarter miles, and District Spirit, a winner at 7 furlongs. His dam was a 2-year-old winner at 6 furlongs and also performed well at a mile. The Kubler stable is currently in good form, and jockey Richard Kingscote is riding impressively with a 17% win rate. At odds of 25/1, an each-way bet appears to be a worthwhile investment.

Finished 10 of 12 in debut run at Kempton back in March of this year. Although not much ability was shown in that race, I do think the sire (Muhaarar (GB)) might have a positive impact, like when winning with 66/1 Shatha a few years back.

Most of the runners are badly out of form, but Gincident won at Leicester on stable debut for James Owen 2 weeks ago. He has won 3 times on AW, including twice here, and is 5lbs below that last winning mark. He looks likely to follow up.

Winner at Newcastle on New Year's Day. Fairly consistent efforts since, with the best of which coming when 2nd off this mark at Southwell last time. Something similar should put him bang there once again.
Was 7 lbs higher when winning for the 4th time last summer. Has been a little disappointing since, but holds an each-way chance if rediscovering some form.

Veteran now in his 97th run on the all-weather, HARBOUR VISION is handily drawn and well handicapped to potentially stick around here. Picked up a couple of wins here in November so there's still some recent form to suggest this 10 year-old might not be done winning just yet. Getting more unpredictable but not without a chance.

A few fingers were burnt backing I'll Give It A Go last time when turned over at short odds on a handicap qualifier. She is still maturing, and that run can be forgiven. Harry Davies takes over the reins today as she makes her handicap debut over a slightly further distance off a mark of just 67. With a couple making their seasonal return, I'll Give It A Go can compensate.

Silent Affair was well held over C&D last time but had shown a bit more in earlier novice runs. She’s not out of it if bouncing back to that better form and could outrun double figure odds if things go her way.

Slowdownbarney won for the first time at the 16th attempt last week. He had been placed in his 4 previous starts, so the win was expected. Although he is 7 lbs higher, he won by nearly 5 lengths over course and distance, so he can follow up.
Moon Over The Sea looked good. Hope they win this time out and have plenty of weight in hand on the market leader, so they can go closer than the odds suggest.

I am not sure if Laser Focus is owned by card players or bridge builders, either way, when the money is down a good run can be expected and this one is quite positive early. He has come down 7 pounds in the weights since the start of the year and steps up in distance. He has bags of stamina (won over hurdles) and also flat speed at a mile and half (won at Lingfield and Brighton last year). A return to class 6 grade is another positive. A nice each way angle with 3 places on offer in a field of 7.

Now on the same mark as when winning at Kempton last summer, and they look to have a winnable race. Plenty of decent runs, including numerous placed efforts since the win. The stable has had a recent winner from only a handful of runners. Jockey's seven-pound claim looks significant.
I am taking a chance with this horse. Definitely not the best, but it shows its best form at this track. If ridden prominently today, it could do okay.
Saffredi won here in October when turned to this shorter distance and subsequently returning from a 6 months break, 12 days ago. So today, it can be expected to complete a hat-trick in C&D.
Kensington Angel runs here under a penalty but has the scope for improvement and can definitely go in close again. Slight each way value.

Three decent runs here over this trip on the last three starts including a win in February. That was despite a few in running issues and due a bit of luck today. Only had fourteen starts so still open to improvement. Looks capable of winning off this mark which is nine pounds below the mark of the only turf run at Bath.

Winner at Chelmsford in December. Solid efforts in defeat since, including when only beaten half a length in 3rd last time. I can't see any reason why he shouldn't run very well once again this evening.

Temperamental horse with vibes of being unreliable, and stats make for grim reading with just one win from 28 runs. But crucially, that win was fairly recent at this course at the start of this month and now much closer to the last winning mark.

MISS MOONSHINE looks to have been dismissed a little too readily here when you consider she's placed on the last two runs over this trip from around this handicap mark. Hasn't been quite as effective on polytrack of late, so you can dismiss the run at Lingfield last time out. Could fare better returning to the tapeta.

Not in the best of form, but is a 2-time C&D winner. Just hoping a return back to this course off a mark much lower than the last winning mark and helped by a drop down in class makes him a credible selection with the price on offer.
Royal Accord for Ian Williams and Warren Fentiman should take all the beating in an effort to win again and should follow up here.

Trust Sergei showed definite improvement on handicap debut here over 6f, racing a bit freely but sticking on well. The drop to 5f looks worth a try and with that recent run under his belt, he’s got a chance of getting involved if settling better early.

Hidden Verse did too much early at Newcastle and paid for it late, but the drop back to 5f could help sharpen her up. She’s got a bit to find on recent form but with the yard in decent nick, there’s a chance she runs better than her odds suggest.

Ran well to finish third over C&D in February and wasn't beaten far when finishing just outside the places in fifth over the same trip at Newcastle last month but was well beaten over the same trip at Southwell a fortnight ago. Return to today's surface should help. Cian Horgan's in good form and his 5lb claim should come in useful. Should be involved at the finish.

BABY ROVER has improved in this sphere in 2023 and was only narrowly beaten by a couple of lengths on the Tapeta at Southwell last time out. Got within a length of short-priced Wee Mary, who is now a couple of pounds heavier in the weights, so the big price discrepancy between the two is surprising.
Amber Waves shaped nicely on debut when placing and receiving weight all around. Can go close again today. Three places each way.

This horse cost nearly twice as much as the favorite (Wondering Why) here, and the trainer is one that I particularly like in Bumpers. This season, for example, he's won with 4 of his 14 runners in this sphere, and this French-bred looks a real contender on breeding since he's closely related to some decent types. The booking of Freddie Mitchell to take another 3lb off is another positive.

This doesn't look like the strongest of bumpers and with the Skeltons record in these races, Johnny Hooves looks to have a good chance. The stable jockey has gone to Haydock chasing the money for his brother in the trainers championship, but Kielan Woods is a more than able deputy and he has ridden numerous winners for the stable. The Skeltons horses are often decent prices in the morning and if fancied they tend to be backed late on, so the 4/1 seems generous.
Looked a decent filly when winning on bumper debut in December. Form franked with 3rd home winning easily next time. Out of her depth in listed race next time and back to calmer waters here.
A few runners have raced and had fair efforts but not convincing. I fancy a big run from the debutant Saint Terry, a progeny of Galileo, as a value each way bet.

Taking a chance with this one as this is a quicker turnaround than between any of the wins. Unexposed at the trip and seems okay on the ground. Jumps okay but sees out the trip well based on the last run.

The race simulation by the model I run suggests Moonset to come in first, ahead of Barricane in second and Coconut Twist in third. Moonset sets for this 3m 2f trip without much prior experience at this distance, compared to Coconut Twist who has won course and distance here as little as 9 days ago. Moonset comes here with good form and looks to extend the winning run here over the longer distance, having not yet finished below second in the handicap hurdle.
Copshill Lad has run at a consistent level for a while. Looked good for a third last time out, and this isn't quite as challenging an affair, so should at least place.
Barricane won on soft with Lewis in the saddle last time out. Although up 4 lbs for that, Lewis is still on top but claiming 7 lbs this time, which I think could help the cause in this C4.

Christopher Wood ran his best race for some time last time out and reverts to hurdles for the first time since 2022 when he was running in top-class races off marks of 141+ (Including 2nd at Ascot in aclass 2). Not done well over fences, although he has shown he can get this trip. With his favoured soft ground anticipated, looking in good heart, this makes him offer some value at 14/1.

Track regular and usual firm ground holds no fears. Last won here in August by 2.75L on firm going. 3/9 on good/firm last time out 3 weeks ago after 3 months off. Apprentice race for one of the track's top trainers.

Alashos has immediately caught my attention here and for very good reason was last seen at Nottingham 8 day's ago where finishing a respectable 3rd/7 over the 6 furlong trip drops in trip here going over the 5 furlong trip that being a wise move by his connections as this very speedy individual can be very effective over this sprinting distance now racing on very suitable turf track that can greatly suit this speedy individual the blinkers are applied for the first time and they can have a positive effect currently operating on an unchanged mark of 69 James Horton's gelded son of showcasing is likely to put up a very bold showing front running performance and will be hard to get past here at the Bath track given his nature of going jockey A J Farragher takes the ride and can give this his best shot bold showing is anticipated and he is certainly one to consider to take this class 5 handicap

Undoubtedly the best horse in the race. Has Cobden on board who's in fine form. Mullins will want as much of this decent-sized pot as possible and swerved Newmarket to be here instead. 3L 3rd to Kargese is very strong form and would be surprised to see him lose this.
